statements.venue: Press release introducing the Make Data Centers Pay Act
statements.quote: As data centers and artificial intelligence drive growing demand for electricity, we need to make sure the companies benefiting from that growth pay their fair share.
statements.context: Introducing a bill requiring large data centers to pay the full incremental cost of their electricity use so households do not.
statements.reason: About AI-driven electricity costs and data centers, which the rubric places out of scope for catastrophic risk.

slowdown.note: No statement found; his data center bills are about electricity costs, not risks from AI itself.

record: Introduced the Make Data Centers Pay Act, requiring data centers of 20 megawatts or more to pay the incremental cost of their electricity use (cost-of-living bill, not AI safety).
Supported legislation ending tax breaks for data center construction, framed around utility costs.

Sponsored the AI Sovereignty Act of 2025 (H.R. 5288), part of a tech-leadership package directing the Commerce Department to track offshore AI development (competition and supply chains, not AI safety).
AIP bill profile and House press release, 10 and 24 September 2025

Sponsored the China AI Threat Assessment Act of 2025 (H.R. 6909, introduced 18 December 2025) and the China AI Power Report Act of 2025 (H.R. 6275, advanced by House Foreign Affairs Committee 21 January 2026); both concern competition with China, not catastrophic AI risk.
grade_reason: His only AI remark found in 2026 is about data centers and electricity bills, and his AI bills concern competition with China; nothing on catastrophic AI risk was found.
